body:
This can technically be circumvented by calling the thirdparty code directly, as the thirdparty folder doesn't have any concept of encapsulation violation & never had the same "can safely remove from the repo completely" guarantee as modules

Granted, that's still messy, and arguably exposes just how much our thirdparty indirection needs to be re-examined

Perhaps in these cases, we want to be able to define module dependencies?

For now, we could also ignore `modules/` until we figure this out.

Modules are in a weird spot, because they seem to want to dynamically insert themselves into different encapsulation levels, but are locked into a singular encapsulation level already. With more and more parts of the codebase getting the ability to be toggled at buildtime (drivers in particular), I don't think the whole separation aspect of modules holds the same significance it  once did

I don't want to ignore them though. This PR is about identifying breakage in encapsulation as it's currently defined, and making it obvious where these discrepancies exist is important if we want to eventually move to a new system

I think there are a number of cases that are more obviously solvable by moving editor code for example to the modules, like has been done with navigation, that would help improve compile behavior and code organization anyway

But I think it'd be good to perhaps split `module` into two categories, one being properly self contained "modules", and the other being toggleable components that usually depends on thirdparty code but is meant to be used in the engine broadly, the problem for that would be how to handle compile order etc. of that

Actually, is this include breaking encapsulation?

My understanding is that we want higher levels to include things from lower levels, but not the other way around. So, this is a module (level 7 in the script) including something from a platform (level 6 in the script). Shouldn't that be OK?

The order from the linked issue is outdated, it's:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a4607f45227d7179e8979d5bd8288461e8e00de9/SConstruct#L1172-L1185

Individual platforms are at the very bottom, though it might be hard to differentiate universal platform code from specific
